name: BLUE OYSTER

plan.note: share of the old 100-bag split; scaled to the 130-bag run, split not yet confirmed

blurb: THE STAPLE. FASTEST TURNAROUND OF THE PLAN.

overview.v: Oysters are the genus Pleurotus. Species share growth biology and differ mainly in colour and preferred temperature.
Easy and forgiving: colonises almost anything. Can reach fruiting readiness in complete darkness.
POCNS is Cap n Stem's house blue oyster code. They keep it despite stroma because its 3-4 lb yields pay.
Steel Blue strain comes out near white when warm and deep blue when cold.
Middle to bottom of the rack.

cultivation.v: Master's Mix: 50:50 red oak sawdust : soybean hulls. Highest-yielding mix, also richest and most fickle.
Calcium carbonate 1-4% reported to raise yield; too much adds heat or stickiness.
One 6 lb (2.7 kg) G2 per twenty 10 lb (4.5 kg) blocks, about 3%.
PDYA to revive a stored culture.
About 10-12 days. Opaque white around day 7. Hold 1-2 more weeks before fridge or use.

timeline.v: About 10-14 days (10 lb block, clear bag). Pins straight away unless refrigerated.
About day 11-12 for blocks. Marks the end of colonisation.
Middle of the 5-15 day range: slower than shiitake and pioppino, faster than chestnut.

climate.v: About 19 °C (66 °F) for blocks, about 18 °C (65 °F) for grain. Prevents stroma in aggressive blue strains.
About 22 °C (72 °F). The 10 lb ultra-pasteurized house block is the 19 °C one.
Keep low. High CO2 gives long stems with no caps.
None needed in incubation. Blocks reach fruiting readiness in the dark.

yield_.v: About 2 lb (0.9 kg) per 10 lb block.
About 4 lb for "other oysters" (block size not stated). 40 blocks gave 80-100 lb, about 2-2.5 lb each.

hazards.v: Hits Pleurotus hardest, blue oysters and kings especially. Warm rooms drive it. Early sign: the centre pin of a cluster, or aborted pins.
150-250 ppm bleach in humidifier water. Switch strain when blotch targets one.
About 99% starts in the grain spawn. Spreads every expansion, cannot be cut out. Prevent with whole grade-1 grain, short of bursting, and correct spawn timing.
A clade attacks Pleurotus: deformed fruit, essentially untreatable.
Spore load matters for staff health. Selecting phenotypes reduces it.

notes.v: Use a CO2 controller on the fruit-room exhaust and read stem length and cap shape as your airflow gauge.
Do not leave colonized blocks or spawn sitting. Refrigerate or fruit promptly or they pin.
Blue ran 27% better and 2.5 days faster in warm months (their rooms are air conditioned).
